summary: Feed s175_triple to 10Gbps NDR is degraded: 230% microburst overload (22.97 Gbps), 17% duplicates, and 93% encrypted bytes exceed 90% tolerance. Tool is dropping bursts and blind to payloads.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is feeding aggregated bursts up to 22.97 Gbps into a single 10 Gbps NDR port (230% of capacity, 2 overloaded 1ms intervals). No load balancing or burst shaping is configured, so tool ingress buffers overflow.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR drops packets during bursts, breaking TCP reassembly and flow tracking; creates blind spots where attacks in burst windows are missed and detection coverage is incomplete.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3x10G NDR ports/instances with 5-tuple hashing to absorb 23 Gbps peaks and keep per-port utilization <80%, preventing burst drops while preserving flow symmetry for NDR.

findings.root_cause: 17% duplicate packets (1796/10569) indicates overlapping SPAN/TAP sources aggregated without deduplication - same flow mirrored from multiple points and forwarded to one tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes ~17% CPU/storage reprocessing identical packets, inflates flow counts and alerts, skews analytics and reduces effective detection capacity.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (hash-based, 5ms window) before delivery to remove identical packets from overlapping feeds while preserving unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: 93% of bytes are encrypted vs NDR tolerance of 90% - traffic mix is predominantly TLS/encrypted with no decrypted mirror being supplied to the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR limited to metadata/JA3 and flow analysis; cannot inspect payloads for IDS signatures, malware, or C2, severely reducing detection coverage despite needing full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Provide selective out-of-band TLS decryption/mirror (or feed from TLS-intercept proxy) for relevant VLANs so NDR receives cleartext payload where policy allows, restoring payload-based detection.
